title: Power Pages: first-class support for Power Platform connector APIs
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and the cited documentation for the general governance controls. It distinguishes existing Power Pages licensing and server logic from the planned connector capability, whose additional licensing, default state and specific controls remain undocumented.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the planned native connector API capability.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "native" "connector" "APIs"; "Power Pages" "connector APIs" licensing default control. Read results and opened learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/configure/server-logic-overview; results describe other integration mechanisms, not this capability.

claims.claim: The default state of native connector API support is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connector APIs first class support connectors SQL SAP Oracle gateway preview March 2027 licensing default enable; "Power Pages" "connector APIs" licensing default control. Read roadmap and server-logic-overview; neither gives this feature's default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Additional licensing and premium connector tier requirements specific to native Power Pages connector APIs are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "connector" "licensing" "gateway"; "Power Pages" "connector APIs" licensing default control. Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-flow-licensing-faq#power-pages; it documents site licensing, not native connector API additions.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Gateway hosting charges and detailed gateway requirements specific to native connector APIs are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "connector" "licensing" "gateway". Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-flow-licensing-faq#power-pages; read wp-onpremises-gateway search excerpts. No native connector API gateway hosting charge or detailed requirement is stated.

claims.claim: Additional capacity charges specific to native connector APIs are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "connector APIs" licensing default control; "Power Pages" "connector" "licensing" "gateway". Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-flow-licensing-faq#power-pages; no native connector API-specific capacity charge is stated.

claims.claim: Power Pages website licensing is capacity based with two capacity types based on user type.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type

claims.claim: One Power Pages capacity type is Authenticated users per website/month.
claims.quote: Authenticated users per website/month

claims.claim: The other Power Pages capacity type is Anonymous users per website/month.
claims.quote: Anonymous users per website/month

claims.claim: A general data policy can be created in Power Platform admin center through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy.
claims.quote: select Security, and then on the Security pane, select Data and privacy. ... On the Data protection and privacy page, select Data policy. ... select New Policy to create a new policy to configure.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy creates a general data policy from the supplied policy object.
claims.quote:
New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy
Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn does not yet confirm how general data policies apply to native Power Pages connector APIs.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connectors APIs data policies endpoint filtering control enable disable Power Platform CLI pac pages Dataverse. Opened wp-data-loss-prevention and advanced-connector-policies on Learn; neither describes native Power Pages connector APIs.

claims.claim: General connector endpoint filtering is configured within a data policy through Prebuilt Connectors > connector > Configure connector > Connector endpoints.
claims.quote: The Endpoint configurable column on the Prebuilt Connectors page in Data Policies indicates whether the endpoint filtering capability is supported for the connector. ... right-clicking and then selecting Configure connector > Connector endpoints.

claims.claim: The printed New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations call creates endpoint filtering configurations for a general data policy.
claims.quote: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId $TenantId -PolicyName $PolicyName -NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations $ConnectorConfigurations

claims.claim: Connector endpoint filtering is a preview feature.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: Endpoint filtering is available where the Endpoint configurable column is Yes.
claims.quote: If the value of the Endpoint configurable column is Yes, you can use this capability by right-clicking and then selecting Configure connector > Connector endpoints.

claims.claim: The documented designer endpoint filtering evaluates static endpoints.
claims.quote: Only static endpoints that are known and selected when building an app, flow, or chatbot during design time are enforced.

claims.claim: The documented designer endpoint rules do not enforce filtering on dynamically bound runtime endpoints.
claims.quote: Endpoint filtering rules aren't enforced on environment variables, custom inputs, and dynamically bound endpoints during runtime.

claims.claim: Learn has not confirmed endpoint filtering applicability to native Power Pages connector APIs.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages native connectors APIs data policies endpoint filtering control enable disable Power Platform CLI pac pages Dataverse. Opened connector-endpoint-filtering and wp-data-loss-prevention on Learn; neither documents native Power Pages connector applicability.

claims.claim: No Power Pages-specific native connector API control is yet documented on the UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "native connectors" "enable" "Dataverse" "API". Read pac pages and Power Pages admin API search excerpts; opened server-logic-overview. No UI, CLI, Dataverse or admin API control specific to native connector APIs is documented.

claims.claim: Per-visitor delegation for the planned native connector capability is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "native connectors" "authorization". Read enhanced Dataverse authorization search excerpts and opened server-logic-overview; neither documents per-visitor delegation for the planned native connector capability.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Enforcement of per-visitor authorisation for native connector API data is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "native connectors" "authorization". Read Dataverse authorization excerpts; opened power-pages-security and server-logic-overview. These describe general security, not per-visitor authorisation of native connector API data.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports POST to send new data to external systems.
claims.quote: POST | function post() { } | Create records or send new data. | Commonly used to insert new records into Dataverse or send data to external systems.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports PUT to replace or update records.
claims.quote: PUT | function put() { } | Replace or update records. | Updates or replaces an entire record or dataset. Typically used for full updates or synchronization scenarios.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports PATCH for partial record updates.
claims.quote: PATCH | function patch() { } | Updates part of a record (upsert). | Performs a partial update of existing data without replacing the entire record.

claims.claim: General Power Pages server logic supports DELETE to remove records or data from an external system.
claims.quote: DELETE | function del() { } | Delete records or fields. | Removes records or data from Dataverse or an external system.

claims.claim: Supported operations for the planned native connector capability are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "native" "connector" "APIs". Read results and opened learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/configure/server-logic-overview; its methods describe general server logic, not the planned native connector capability's supported operations.

claims.claim: Power Pages sites are available to internal users by default.
claims.quote: By default, all Power Pages sites are available to users who are internal to your organization.

claims.claim: The public site visibility setting permits anonymous internet access.
claims.quote: The public setting makes the site accessible to everyone over the Internet anonymously or to users authenticated through identity providers.
